documents.title: Our Mission
content: About Our Mission Home / About Us Who We Are A Socio-economic, Environmental & Humanitarian Membership Association Teamenvironment.KE.Africa is focused on Greening and Environmental Conservation through inclusive, community-based action. We believe that sustainable development starts with local commitment.

Our Association is dedicated to addressing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and protecting Kenya's diverse landscapes from the impacts of climate change. Join Our Community Our Vision To be the leading champion in environmental conservation and humanitarian services, creating a greener and more sustainable future for all Kenyans.
Our Mission To foster climate change adaptation and mitigation by catalyzing community-level interventions that enhance well-being, livelihood security, and environmental conservation.

Our Philosophy “Build a Heritage for Future Generations of a Cleaner, Greener (Food & Water) Secure and a Peaceful Environment.” 32+ Completed Projects 1,520+ Partners & Colleagues 121+ Registered Members 47 Counties Reached Our History The Reforestation Journey From humble roots in 2021 to a nationwide green network, see how our Green Army is transforming landscapes year by year.

2021 Founding & Humble Roots Teamenvironment.KE.Africa is founded with a handful of visionary conservationists and establishes its first community seed propagation nurseries in Nairobi. 2022 KFS Strategic Partnership TEK signs a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), adopting key degraded acreage within the Ngong Hills ecosystem for active rehabilitation.

2023 50,000 Seedlings Milestone The Green Army mobilizes local communities, successfully propagating and planting over 50,000 indigenous trees while establishing two community agroforestry hubs. 2024 Greening Digital Platform Launch of our modern, offline-ready progressive web app (PWA) allowing volunteers, members, and supporters to easily track and book reforestation outings.

2025 150,000+ Trees & Automation Crossing the 150,000 trees mark. Integrated automated payment gateways (M-Pesa, PayPal, PesaPal) providing immediate Certificates of Impact and receipts to digital supporters globally.
2026 Live Stewardship Hub Unveiling the dynamic Stewardship Wall of Fame, progress milestones, and custom footprint certificate previews to maximize transparency and community engagement.

Question 1 of 5 Score: 0/0 Why are indigenous trees (like Acacia) preferred over exotic species (like Eucalyptus) in water catchment areas? Why?

Indigenous trees absorb less water and retain local aquifers, preserving streamflows, unlike Eucalyptus which has extremely high transpiration rates and can dry out catchments. documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT KENYA
content: In Kenya (TEAMENVIRONMENT KENYA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 150,000 trees planted, 5,000 volunteers, 2,500 acres restored, and 32 projects. The heart of Teamenvironment.KE.Africa. Hosting our core restoration projects in the Ngong Hills Ecosystem, Nyeri watersheds, and urban greening initiatives across Nairobi and Nakuru. The goals for Kenya are: Plant 15 billion trees by 2032 and increase national canopy cover to 30% through community agroforestry.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT UGANDA
content: In Uganda (TEAMENVIRONMENT UGANDA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 85,000 trees planted, 2,800 volunteers, 1,200 acres restored, and 14 projects. Working in the Mabira Forest and Mount Elgon regions to restore degraded forest ecosystems and establish community nurseries that support sustainable smallholder farming. The goals for Uganda are: Restore 50,000 hectares of degraded forest reserve and empower 10,000 women through fruit tree nursery ownership.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT TANZANIA
content: In Tanzania (TEAMENVIRONMENT TANZANIA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 95,000 trees planted, 3,100 volunteers, 1,600 acres restored, and 18 projects. Leading efforts in Kilimanjaro forest restoration and dryland regreening in Dodoma using sustainable FMNR (Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration) techniques. The goals for Tanzania are: Establish green corridors around the Mount Kilimanjaro slopes and restore crucial water catchment zones.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT RWANDA
content: In Rwanda (TEAMENVIRONMENT RWANDA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 60,000 trees planted, 2,200 volunteers, 950 acres restored, and 11 projects. Partnering with local cooperatives to combat soil erosion on hillside farms using high-density agroforestry and bamboo planting along riverbanks. The goals for Rwanda are: Secure 100% soil stabilization across pilot mountainous terraced areas and protect the Gishwati-Mukura national forest.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT ETHIOPIA
content: In Ethiopia (TEAMENVIRONMENT ETHIOPIA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 110,000 trees planted, 4,500 volunteers, 2,100 acres restored, and 22 projects. Focused on the drylands of Tigray and the southern highlands, restoring watersheds to increase ground-water recharge and agricultural yield. The goals for Ethiopia are: Plant 10 million native seedlings and restore 5 large degraded sub-watershed basins.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT NIGERIA
content: In Nigeria (TEAMENVIRONMENT NIGERIA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 125,000 trees planted, 6,200 volunteers, 2,800 acres restored, and 25 projects. Combating desertification in the north through the Great Green Wall Initiative and restoring mangrove forests in the Niger Delta to protect coastal biodiversity. The goals for Nigeria are: Reforest 10,000 hectares of coastal mangroves and hold back desert encroachment in northern border states.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT GHANA
content: In Ghana (TEAMENVIRONMENT GHANA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 75,000 trees planted, 3,400 volunteers, 1,400 acres restored, and 15 projects. Restoring cocoa agroforestry systems in the Ashanti region and executing clean-water access projects through riparian vegetation restoration. The goals for Ghana are: Transit 5,000 smallholder cocoa farms to organic agroforestry models and protect local river headwaters.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT SENEGAL
content: In Senegal (TEAMENVIRONMENT SENEGAL), TEAMEnvironment is active with 55,000 trees planted, 2,100 volunteers, 1,100 acres restored, and 9 projects. Leading major mangrove reforestation in the Casamance region and establishing community-managed windbreaks in dry, dusty northern farmlands. The goals for Senegal are: Restore 2,000 hectares of estuaries and provide training in smart saline-agriculture to 15 rural women groups.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT IVORY COAST
content: In Ivory Coast (TEAMENVIRONMENT IVORY COAST), TEAMEnvironment is active with 65,000 trees planted, 2,400 volunteers, 1,250 acres restored, and 12 projects. Focused on the recovery of degraded national parks and introducing sustainable agroforestry practices to cocoa-producing communities in the western belt. The goals for Ivory Coast are: Plant 1.5 million native shade trees on commercial cocoa farms to protect soil quality and natural microclimates.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT EGYPT
content: In Egypt (TEAMENVIRONMENT EGYPT), TEAMEnvironment is active with 45,000 trees planted, 1,900 volunteers, 800 acres restored, and 8 projects. Utilizing treated wastewater to establish forest plantations in desert soils (Serapium Forest) and implementing urban forestry in Cairo to combat pollution. The goals for Egypt are: Afforest 500 acres of desert borderlands with hardy species and establish vertical green walls in dense urban settings.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT MOROCCO
content: In Morocco (TEAMENVIRONMENT MOROCCO), TEAMEnvironment is active with 70,000 trees planted, 2,900 volunteers, 1,500 acres restored, and 13 projects. focused on argan forest restoration in the Atlas mountains and creating green belts around major royal cities to prevent sand encroachment. The goals for Morocco are: Revitalize 3,000 hectares of argan and carob orchards, empowering local Berber women cooperatives.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT ALGERIA
content: In Algeria (TEAMENVIRONMENT ALGERIA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 50,000 trees planted, 1,800 volunteers, 1,000 acres restored, and 10 projects. Part of the historic Green Dam initiative, planting rows of pine and cypress trees to arrest desertification and sand movement toward the northern fertile lands. The goals for Algeria are: Reconstruct 1,200 km of robust green shelterbelts and establish local forest fire warning community networks.

documents.title: TEAMENVIRONMENT TUNISIA
content: In Tunisia (TEAMENVIRONMENT TUNISIA), TEAMEnvironment is active with 40,000 trees planted, 1,600 volunteers, 750 acres restored, and 7 projects. focused on restoring olive groves and native ecosystems in the semi-arid regions of central Tunisia to protect smallholder farmers from desert climate swings. The goals for Tunisia are: Plant 500,000 dryland olive trees and scale community rainwater harvesting techniques in 5 major municipalities.

documents.title: NGONG’ HILLS RESTORATION PROJECT 2026.docx
content: OUR REF: TEK/NG’HCM/003 DATE: 29/10/2025 CLIMATE ACTORS, ENVIRONMENT STAKEHOLDERS and conservation partners NAIROBI. Dear Sir/Madam, RE: NGONG’ HILLS RESTORATION PROJECT, “TREE PLANTING (GROWING) EXPEDITION” ECO-TOURISM EDITION. The Environment is a vital component of our existence.
We therefore need a concerted and collaborative efforts to Protect, Preserve, Rehabilitate and Restore it at ALL COST.

Besides providing resources to humanity, our very life and existence is sustained virtually by the environment, this therefore behooves us in spite of country and regional boundaries to do anything and everything within our means and power that is humanly possible to CONSERVE IT not just for ourselves but for posterity.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA has been allocated 6.2HA (15Acres) by the Kenya Forest Service of the Degraded Ngong Hills which is an important catchment area, one of the Water Towers for Adoption so that we can Protect, Conserve, Restore and Rehabilitate It. Genesis 2:15 (Verse 5). This is in our quest to combat Climate Change and mitigate on the devastating effects of Global Warming, SDG NO.
13 as well as increase the Forest and Tree Cover in support of the governments’ commitment to Plant (Grow) at least #15 Billion Trees by 2032.

In view of the above, we are inviting and requesting you (your organizations, company and institution) to Partner, Support and Participate in the Ngong Hills Conservation Mission, during which we shall be conducting a Twenty (20) Thousand Tree Planting (Growing) Expedition.

All Participants, (Parents and their Children) and schools and Institutions will be accorded an Opportunity to Interact with Nature by Planting Seedlings Equivalent to their Age Under Our Initiative #Trees4Birthday - March and April Born Babies. DATE: - Wed 18th, Thu 19th, Friday 20th March 2026. TIME: - 9am – 3.30pm daily.

content: Who is ‘TEAMEnvironment KENYA’ TEAMEnvironment KENYA is a Socio-economic and Environmental Association which constitutes of registered membership, volunteers and representatives from corporate organizations, social enterprises, youth and women groups and organizations (public and private), SCHOOLS, INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER LEARNING, NGO’s, CBO’s, Foundations and community members and other institutions who are focused on Greening and Environmental Conservation as a means to reversing the effects of global warming and CLIMATE CHANGE.

The Organization is committed on addressing itself on SDG No. 13 by (Climate Action), ensuring habitable environment SDG No. 15 (Life on Land) and SDG No. 2 (Zero Hunger) by promoting sustainable environmental practices so as to ensure Food Security.

The philosophy of “Leaving a Heritage for Future Generations of a Cleaner, Greener (Food & Water) Secure Environment of FLORA, FAUNA & AQUATIC LIFE.” underscores our mandate, duty and responsibility to make (and be) the desired change towards green lifestyles in an endeavor to address ourselves to the various components of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This will ensure green and clean homes, workplaces, communities, towns, counties, countries and to ultimately find lasting solutions within our ‘environments’ towards a habitable “planet Earth” now and for posterity.

WHAT WE DO We are involved in reforestation, agro-forestry, conservation agriculture and tree planting activities, as well as other best greening and environmental practices that espouse private public community partnerships in environmental conservation, resource management, restoration and biodiversity protection at community level.

Our main goal is to contribute to the legacy of a habitable, peaceful, green, and clean environment for all, now and in posterity. Vision To be the most resourceful national network of cross-sector and multi-stakeholder actors committed to creating a green legacy in the conservation and protection of biodiversity and ecosystem services enhancement.

Mission To foster climate change adaptation and mitigation by catalyzing community-level interventions that enhances well-being, livelihood security, environmental conservation and sustainable asset-based community development.

Core Values The core guiding principles for the achievement of the TEK Mission are individual and organizational virtues including the following among many others: Integrity: All engagements are based on honesty, transparency and accountability. Inclusivity: An all-hands-on-deck model of participatory involvement of primary and secondary stakeholders in sustainable development.

Environmental Responsibility: individual and shared responsibility, to reduce the environmental carbon footprint through established ecological goals, and in following through on environmental commitments.

Commitment to Legacy: To inspire community level adoption of green lifestyles and integrating environmental best practices into sustainable activities that conserve biodiversity and help secure ecosystem services for the future as a legacy.

Livelihood Support: commitment to enhancing the safety, health and well-being of the members by implementing solution-oriented activities in their areas of engagement. TEK’s main objectives are to:- Promote a network of the local youth and community workforce into CBOs and groups that engage in sustainable development.

We engage through issue-based approaches towards employing localized solutions in implementing sustainable people-focused and environment-centric endeavors. Establish sustainable value-chains and green job opportunities from climate-smart food and agricultural/commercial/industrial products from comprehensively efficient natural resource management.

Sustain cooperation between members and constituent groups while ensuring their autonomy, diversity of activities, dynamism of their ideas, representation of their collective interests and the success of self-empowerment, enhancement and development.

Establish a resource centre through which youth and communities gain access to information for analysis, evaluation and dissemination; get vocational/academic training; and other tools they might use in the pursuit of excellence including support planning, funding, development management and growth of their enterprise.

Coordinate small-holder households, individual micro-entrepreneurs, youth groups, community enterprises and youth-focused formal organizations committed to social, economic and environmental sustainability especially to the base of the pyramid (BOP).

Promote sustained collaboration with relevant and value-adding cross-sector stakeholders and discourage the unsustainable exploitation of resources and unfair exploitation of community resources at the expense of base of the pyramid societies.

Foster accountability among local, regional and national leadership structures by highlighting pertinent, viable, sustainable and ethical issues that need addressing for sustainable development. Help create a new one billion shillings micro-economy among community micro-entrepreneurs.
Establishing a national coalition of greening and social enterprise associations operating country-wide and linking internationally.

A membership and partnership strategy has been developed that takes into consideration the various classes of stakeholders including volunteers, individual community members, CBOs, students and their societies/clubs, different types of learning/training institutions, corporate entities, civil societies, county and national government agencies, international organizations, media and other stakeholders.

TEK’s main roles to members are:- Establishing contacts with stakeholders and programme development activities; Designing of projects and activities in collaboration with development partners, and other project initiating stakeholders including government to facilitate member participation through mobilization towards success in implementation.

Offering of Support Services in the design and handling of action plans, proposals and other documentation. Facilitation in the establishment and implementation of operations through a suitable cooperative movement. Facilitation in the acquisition of property, land and other capital resources for the organization’s strategic investments such as eco-camps.

Instituting a member information (ICT) and material resource centers. Facilitating member training in liaison with relevant stakeholders and extension services providers. Conducting and tabling of monitoring and evaluation reports on behalf of the Board and TEK members. TEAMEnvironment KENYA will engage in environmental conservation activities in all counties across the country and in the region.

The events will be undertaken in rural, urban, peri-urban areas, including residential and commercial environments. Other environmental activities and expeditions include:- Tree planting for sensitization and mobilization on reforestation, afforestation and agro-forestry/woodlots. Town-cleaning. River(s) adoption and rehabilitation. Wetland reclamation. Restoration of our water towers.

Fundraising for conservation through nature walks, cycling, hikes, forest ‘bush whacks’, and media documentaries. Other arranged activities for eco-tourism including game drives, zip-lines, board walks, canopy walks, tree platforms, bird watching bird hides, guided boat tours.

These activities and many others shall be undertaken within Game reserves/parks, forest/nature reserves, marine reserves/parks, wetlands, heritage sites, as well as biosphere reserves. This will inspire change in the way individuals/communities live, work, play and travel in interaction with nature.

Our constituent organizations are already operating across the various sectors including environmental services, housing, manufacturing, health, nutrition/agriculture, transport, education, water services, and many others.

Some of the collaborations will inspire the creation of Eco-camps, demonstration farms/nurseries, Resource Centers and corresponding events/activities dedicated to conservation of the environment with emphasis on developing and managing natural resources and the species of fauna and flora identified as stressed or gazetted as endangered.
These will be placed in our itinerary for all future engagements in partnerships with stakeholders across all counties within Kenya and beyond.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA aims at boosting natural resources, conservation, conservation agriculture, and local eco-tourism, by engaging in all-inclusive participatory activities within communities in planting trees, cleanups, training/learning camps, public sensitization on responsible lifestyles, and travel to conserved natural resource sites, advocacy for the well being of the local community and sustainable development.

The activities will underpin TEK’s various study/conservation expeditions in natural protected areas on land and/or sea. The protection and maintenance of biological diversity and of natural and associated cultural resources is an essential environmental service whose development, implementation, practice is critical to TEK’s mission.

TEK’s liaison with the relevant stakeholders and the managers of the various sites envisions in the short and long term, seeking member participation/ inclusion/ visits on world/national environmental events focusing on resilience of natural or sustainably managed landscapes/seascapes or resource protected areas.

These include protected forests (Highland forests, Dry land forests, Western rainforests, Urban forests, Coastal forests & Mangrove areas, Eastern Arc Mountain forests), national parks, marine parks, nature reserves, national sanctuaries, and world heritage sites.
The aim is to engage all hands on deck among stakeholders in enhancing the sustainable use of natural ecosystems in Kenya, across the region and globally.

Engagement and partnership As a movement comprising of diverse stakeholder interest, TEK has developed a mode of engagement, exchange and partnership embodies a range of activities to take into account the various external collaborators, partners and stakeholders.

TEK works closely with the professionals, business leaders, industry players and the local community members to ensure that the intervention/ mitigation measures are solution-oriented to prevailing environmental challenges. Research and training instill knowledge and skills necessary to innovatively synergize and employ practical solutions to challenges faced in society and the environment.

TEK’s Community and Public Engagements are through: provision of direct services – student volunteerism, student placements/internships in member organizations, provision of specialist services (professional or technical e.g.

legal advice, environmental impact assessments, energy audits, social impact analysis and local content enhancement, GIS and pictorials, media documentaries), provision of specialist skills (ICT, community/ group work), mentoring, life-long learning, free consultancy and support, contribution to governance via umbrella association membership, board membership, trusteeships, and others.

Sustainable development work – contributing to capacity building among communities, collaborating with corporate businesses and social enterprises, work with environmental service consumers and special interest groups, civic partnerships with the public, schools and development organizations.

Engagement in policy and product development and social innovation –research and development, lobby for policy framework development/enforcement at county and national government levels, public services, social enterprises.

Collaboration with communities -engaging in socio-ecological and economic activities, and employing indigenous capacity/local knowledge in developing conservation survey projects and sustainably implementing them through stakeholder collaborations.

Discharging ethical responsibilities – disseminating pertinent triple bottom-line information to community members especially concerning socially sensitive research on, for example, developments in green technologies, impact investments, climate-smart initiatives, among others.

Disseminating information and knowledge development among non-specialist local community members, through events such as camps, public training workshops, public conferences/forums and debates as well as more feedback-generating interactions in public events such as those depicted the United Nations World Environmental Events Calendar.
Producing content for public use, like Media Documentary Reports, performances and social media outputs.

Mobilizing the Green Facility initiative - partnering on PPP frameworks in enhancing sustainable utility and management of physical infrastructure, land-use and water catchment management as a resource management practice Supporting government agendas - liaising on constitutional, legislative, regulatory and policy provisions in relation to socio-economic and environmental issues for public good, through engaging community participants such as CBOs, FBOs, Youths, Women and PWD’s to widen participation in climate-smart practice and sustainable enterprise.

content: Championing Climate Action and Environmental Sustainability towards Achieving 30% T ree and Forest Cover for Stronger Climate Resilience. INTRODUCTION TEAMEnviroment KENY A is a Socio-Economic, Humanitarian Non-governmental Environmental Organization (National Environment and Conservation Movement). The trend setters in conservation on our mission to keep Kenya, Clean, Green and breathing.

Championing the 15 Billlion T ree Growing Agenda. Our T en (10) Million T ree Nursery, Seedling Propagation and Study Center is at the Kabarak University in Nakuru County currently housing 350,000 assorted seedlings ready for planting. We plan to replicate these tree nurseries across the 46 counties through our "SUST AINABLE ENVIRONMENT AL RESTORA TION PROGRAMME" (SERP).

This initiative directly supports President H.E. Dr . William Samoei Ruto's directive on Mashujaa Day, October 20th 2022, and the government's commitment to increase national tree and forest cover to 30% by 2032. This is by growing 15 billion trees by 2032, alongside efforts to secure, rehabilitate, and protect public forests and restore degraded water towers and other forest ecosystems.

Our efforts will significantly help in combating , desertification and climate change; fostering a "GREEN ECONOMY" . This is inline with the government's Climate Action; 15 Billion T ree Growing Agenda. This ambitious target creates substantial employment opportunity for millions of youth and women groups nationwide.

By engaging in agribusiness and agroforestry, they will enhance environmental restoration through massive seedlings propagation, nurturing, and tree growing thereby addressing the current demand of 360 million seedlings per year .

Our Conservation Mission and T rack Record TEAMEnvironment KENY A has consistently championed the Greening Kenya Initiative through its nationwide conservation mission for the past six years. During this period, we successfully planted (grown) over 2.8 million trees across the country in different counties.

A notable achievement includes 10,000-tree planting (growing) expeditions which we conducted in the North Eastern Counties, they include Wajir , Marsabit, Garisa and Isiolo counties where we planted a total of 100,000+ seedlings between 2019 and 2021. This we conducted with the support of the community and the respective county governments.

TEK is committed to reclaiming and rehabilitating degraded landscapes and restoring vital forest resources, benefiting both human and local ecosystems. We achieved this through unique adventure and sporting "Expeditions" across the 47 counties, featuring activities such as mountain climbing, cycling & skating for Climate action and marathon.

These initiatives not only advance environmental conservations but also promote peace, foster social cohesion amongest communities and strengthens co-existence in our national conservation efforts. Our Approach to Climate Action and Environmental Restoration.

Reclaiming Degradable Lands We restore degradable forest lands to improve productivity, enhance food security, reduce povety, conserve soils, protect water towers, and boost biodiversity for human well being. Building Climate Resilience Our initiatives strengthens climate change resilience and adaptation, fostering sustainable development by restoring ecological balance in defforested landscapes.

Multistake Holder Collaborations TEAMEnvironment KENY A patners with the National and County governments environmental agencies they include; KFS, NEMA, KEFRI, KWS. This collaborative effort aims to plant (grow) 100,000,000 trees by 2032, supporting government in achieving 30% national tree and forest cover .

Community Lead Nursery By engaging youth and women groups in the 47 counties,with an aim of establishing a 1 million tree seedlings nursery per county. This nurseries will have assorted seedlings species. Which will include fruit trees indegenious trees, exotic trees and bamboo.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY TEAMEnvironment KENY A is a socio economic, non-governmental environmental membership organization that constitute youth and women organizations, schools & institutions, community members, and other diverse groups. We are dedicated to environmental conservation and greening initiatives, actively combating climate change and mitigating the effects of global warming.

Our philosophy, "Leaving a Heritage for Future Generations, " underscores our unwavering commitment to fostering sustainable lifestyles, effectively addressing environmental challenges, and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This dedication drives our efforts to promote green and clean environments across homes, workplaces, communities, towns, counties, and countries, ensuring a habitable 'Planet Earth' for all generations. TEK serves as a cross-sectoral, multi-stakeholder forum, convening ecosystem conservationists and experts in ecosystem services.

It is supported by a dedicated team of environmental, forestry, and community development professionals, this collaborative framework enables the design and implementation of inclusive and sustainable programs. These programs deliver solutions by integrating biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services management with sustainable community development.

Our programs are built on strong partnerships with county governments, the private sector , civil society, TEK Members (youth and women groups), development agencies, and academic institutions, alongside the inclusive involvement of community members.

A key repeatable model involves establishing T ree Nurseries and Seedling Propagation Centers, followed by T ree Planting (Growing) Expeditions across all 47 counties. This model considers various ecological zones and prioritizes fruit trees, indigenous species, and non-invasive exotic trees with medicinal, cultural, nutritional, ornamental, woody biomass, or ecological significance.

Our 10,000,000 T ree Million Seedlings Initiative. TEAMEnvironment KENY A (TEK) mobilizes an extensive network of over 700 registered members across the 47 counties. These dedicated volunteers are committed to preserving, restoring, and protecting biodiversity4a vital resource for humanity.

With your partnership and support, TEK will seeks establish 1,000,000 tree nurseries throughout the rest of 46 counties, engaging youth, women, and community volunteers in this critical effort. These nurseries will be established in schools, institutions, and on public and private farmlands within various wards and sub-counties.

Local youth and women groups will manage them under a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOUs) and partnership agreements with the respective entities and institutions. TEK actively engages grassroots communities, sensitizing and mobilizing local groups including smallholder households, youth and women groups, community forest associations, CBOs, schools, and social enterprises.

This initiative projects the annual propagation of 10,000 seedlings per nursery from the 50,000 nurseries across the 47 counties, producing over 500 million seedlings per year. Nurseries will receive professional guidance and technical support from KFS and KEFRI extension service officers, with additional supervision and technical assistance provided by TEK and its volunteers.
This initiative aims to rehabilitate and restore riparian areas, wetlands, and gazetted (and yet-to-be-gazetted) Water T owers, collaborating with relevant national and county government agencies.

TEK will ensure best practices for facility management at these nursery resource and seedling propagation centers, incorporating robust monitoring, evaluation, and reporting mechanisms to guarantee program sustainability and success. Vision, Mission & Core Values Vision T o be the premier national network of cross-sector stakeholders, dedicated to forging a lasting green legacy.

We achieve this by conserving, protecting, restoring, rehabilitating and nurturing our vital biodiversity and its essential ecosystem services. Mission T o advance climate change adaptation and mitigation through powerful community resilience initiatives.

These initiatives enhance local knowledge, improve well-being, build sustainable assets, promote green value chains, and drive comprehensive sustainable development. Core Values Our core values define TEK's mission, embodying the individual and organizational principles that guide our work: Integrity Integrity is our foundation.

All engagements are built on honesty, transparency, and accountability. Inclusivity We embrace a participatory model, actively involving all primary and secondary stakeholders to drive sustainable development.

Environmental Responsibility We champion individual and collective responsibility to reduce our environmental footprint, adhering to established ecological goals and unwavering environmental pledges. Commitment to Green Legacy We inspire community-level adoption of green lifestyles and integrate environmental best practices into sustainable activities.

Our goal is to conserve biodiversity and secure ecosystem services for future generations. Livelihood Support We enhance the safety, health, and well-being of our members by implementing solution-oriented activities within their communities and workplaces.

Strategic Objectives & Activities Stakeholder Engagement & Mobilization Launch advocacy and awareness campaigns to empower stakeholders for proactive climate change preparation and response. Foster networking and establish critical linkages among all relevant parties. Capacity Building Develop and deliver effective training programs for trainers, mentors, and change leaders.

Provide specialized greening consultancy services to equip communities with essential tools for localized climate mitigation and adaptation solutions. Driving T ransformative Change Inspire a paradigm shift among stakeholders to embrace green best practices.

Promote climate-smart technologies and engage communities in sustainable natural resource management, enhancing environmental conservation and ecosystem protection. Conflict Resolution & Monitoring Implement effective systems for monitoring, resolving, and reporting human-wildlife conflicts. Develop a digital application for feedback on interactions among humans, wildlife, and natural resources.

Disaster Preparedness & Mitigation Facilitate proactive information sharing and early warning systems for environmental challenges. Mobilize member support and provide livelihood assistance to enhance community disaster preparedness. Operational Formalization Support the registration, documentation, and legalization of TEK member operations.

Facilitate their integration, mainstreaming, and provide business development support to strengthen organizational foundation and impact. Resource Mobilization & Fundraising Implement robust resource mobilization strategies to ensure successful T ree Nursery Establishment and Seedlings Propagation initiatives.

Actively fundraise for conservation and livelihood causes by establishing an impact investing and asset- building platform for smallholder households and stakeholder programs. Promoting Social Entrepreneurship Develop sustainable green value chains by fostering businesses that drive change.

Support sustainable enterprises to benefit households at the base of the pyramid and micro-enterprises, creating positive social and environmental impact. Advocacy & Lobbying Formulate recommendations and lobby policymakers on critical climate change issues. Utilize a dedicated platform to voice concerns regarding environmental degradation, deforestation, and community marginalization.

Actively engage with national, county governments and other stakeholders to advocate for biodiversity conservation and effective ecosystem services management. ST A TEMENT OF NEED & Kenya's Forest Challenge With 80% of its land comprising Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs), Kenya's natural forest resources face immense pressure.

High demand for raw materials, land conversion, infrastructure development, and socio-economic challenges like poverty drive this threat. Forests, vital for ecosystem balance, biodiversity, and livelihoods, are severely endangered. A notable gap persists between policy discussions on ecosystem services and actual community involvement.

TEAMEnvironment KENY A aims to close this gap by establishing 1,000,000 tree nurseries, seedling propagation, and environmental resource centers across all 47 Kenyan counties, directly engaging and empowering communities. Kenya consumes approximately 80 million trees annually but requires 450 million for sustainable forest management.

This deficit is worsened by a heavy reliance on biomass energy, as charcoal and firewood constitute about 70% of primary energy consumption. Widespread deforestation, degradation, and rampant forest fires have severely impacted critical water towers like Mount Kenya, Mau Forest, and the Aberdare Ranges. Charcoal and firewood collectively account for about 70% of primary energy consumption.

Despite the government's recent ban on illegal logging and forest product extraction, timber scarcity has driven up demand and prices. Biomass energy consumption remains high and is even rising, fueled by poverty, population growth, and urbanization. The illegal charcoal industry, estimated at KES 40 to 80 billion (USD 4003800 million) annually, thrives due to corruption.

This, combined with industrial woody biomass use and overgrazing in the Rift Valley, places immense strain on natural resources and encroaches upon rich biodiversity. Kenya's forest cover plummeted from 20% at independence in 1963 to a mere 2% in the 1990s. While restoration efforts have raised it to 8.2%, this remains below the 10% UN recommended minimum and the 12. 16% global convention target.

Kenya's Vision 2030 aims to plant 360 million trees annually, targeting over 5 million hectares of additional forest cover through the 15 Billion T ree Growing Agenda by 2032. T o achieve this, 70% of new forest cover will result from reforestation, afforestation, and tree farm planting, with the remaining 30% from natural regeneration.

Environmental rights and actions are enshrined in Article 42 of the Constitution of Kenya 2010, alongside other policy frameworks, mandating proactive conservation efforts to meet Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Integrating sustainable forest resource development, management, and conservation is vital for enriching biodiversity and ensuring the provision of essential ecosystem goods and services for domestic and industrial utilization.

Programme Development & Implementation Phase 1: Nursery Establishment We establish nurseries in optimal locations (schools, institutions, public/private lands) with reliable water and security. KFS and KEFRI guide the selection of indigenous, exotic, and non-invasive species for cultural, ornamental, nutritional, medicinal, conservation, and restoration purposes.

Phase 2: Logistics & Support We provide volunteers with meals, transport, and accommodation, ensuring their full participation in nationwide tree planting (growing) across all 47 counties. Emergency services are available as needed throughout the program.

Phase 3: Facility Management TEK collaborates with the local communities to establish and manage tree nurseries and the planting of trees nurturing them to maturity. One million nurseries across the 47 counties will increase the tree and forest cover inline with the TEK's Sustainable Landscape Environment Restoration Program (SLERP) to build climate resilience.

Phase 4: Resource Centre Development Nurseries evolve into resource centers, scaling capacity for diverse plants (trees, shrubs, grasses). These centers serve multiple functions: conservation, carbon sequestration, biomass production, medicinal, cultural, nutritional, fodder , building materials, energy, shade, and ornamental.

We prioritize indigenous and exotic non-invasive species, using local resources to reduce costs. CONCLUSION As TEAMEnvironment KENY A, we are dedicated to leaving a lasting heritage for future generations: a cleaner , greener (food & water) secure, and peaceful environment thriving with diverse flora, fauna, and aquatic life.

This duty, mandate, and conservation responsibility cannot be abdicated or delegated; it rests with all of us. T o this vital cause, our clarion call is: "Let's Go Green With Y ou. " Best Regards, MA THEW OCHANDA EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR Contacts:- +254 718 052 745 | 725 660 204 Social Handles Website. http/ / teamenvironment.org X:- tek_kenya IG/FB,LinkedIn TEAMEnviroment KENY A

INTRODUCTION TEAMEnvironment KENYA seeks to plant (Grow) at least One Hundred (100) Million Trees and shrubs in the 47 Counties by 2032 having established a Ten (10) Million Tree Nursery and seedlings Propagation Centre at the KABARAK UNIVERSITY in Nakuru County our initiative dubbed SLERP, “SUSTAINABLE LANDSCAPE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION PROGRAMME.” This is in response to the Decree by HE.

President. Dr. William Ruto declaration and commitment to significantly increase the counties tree (forest) cover of 8.2 to 30% by 2032. This will significantly contribute to the realization of a, “GREEN ECONOMY” Combat Climate Change and Mitigate the devastating effects of Global Warming.

This new target provides a challenge and an employment opportunity to millions of youth and women groups countrywide as they work towards improving the environment by engaging in agribusiness and agroforestry farming practice. This entails massive seedlings propagation, nurturing and growing of the trees whose demand is now at 360 Million seedlings per year.

In this regard TEK has been on the front row championing and spearhead the GREENING KENYA INITIAVE & Conservation Mission consistently for the last four years now, have planted at least 1Million Trees in various counties.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA has a commitment and determination towards reclamation of degraded landscape and forest resources for the good of humanity and the ecosystems through adventure and sporting activities dubbed, “Expeditions” which involves activities such as, mountain climbing, cycling & skating and running (marathon) in the 47 Counties as we propagate the message of peace and encourage (peaceful coexistence amongst communities) social cohesion and intergression in our county and countrywide conservation initiatives.
This process will improve productivity of the degraded forest lands, improve food security, reduces poverty, enhances climate change, resilience, adaptation and fosters sustainable development.

This exercise presents many new challenges and opportunities in the efforts to conserve soil, our water towers, biodiversity, restore ecological services and facilitate human well-being in and around deforested or degraded forest landscapes.
The tremendous material and human resource requirements, as well as the technical and financial pre-requisites call for cross-sector and multi-stakeholder approach and inclusion.

In our quest and desire to bring change and transformation in our environment and ecosystem countrywide TEAMEnvironment KENYA has been working in partnership and collaboration with the various County Governments and other agencies/organizations at the county level, business communities, schools/institutions and all stakeholders so as to ensure a successful execution and consequent realization of the 10Million Trees planting (growing) target by 2022 in our endeavor to realizing the desired 10% Tree (Forest) Cover.

While forests are an important environmental resource and play a valuable role in not only the balance of ecosystems as a habitat for critical flora, fauna and aquatic life. They enhance the livelihoods of people in communities across the country, the region and beyond.

Kenya consumes about 80 million trees per year, causing a need for 450 million trees annually for the forest resource requirements to be sustainably met. This is due to Kenya’s heavy dependence on biomass energy, deforestation and forest degradation.

The degradation may be due to forest fires, which we have had rampant happenings of in the resent past which adversely affected our Main WATER TOWERS; Mount Kenya, Mau Forest and Aberdare’s Ranges respectively.

This was due to the outstretched drought season and unsustainable charcoal production, poor agricultural expansion activity, overgrazing, poorly planned settlements, excessive extraction of forest resources, or over-cultivation.

Notably, charcoal and firewood account for about 70% of primary energy consumption, and despite the government’s recent ban on illegal logging and extraction of forest products, the demand for timber has gone up due to its scarcity and consequent its price. Biomass energy is still high and rising due to poverty levels, population growth and urbanization.

The biggest incentives to unsustainable charcoal production are also the greatest disincentives to all environmental conservation and ecosystem protection efforts: the annual retail value of the industry is currently estimated between KES 40 to 80 billion (USD 400–800 million) according to the KFS reports.

The charcoal business has continued to thrive, yet it is illegal since no registration has been made for a single charcoal producer association because corruption drives this huge so called ‘black market’ enterprise.

Manufacturers, especially in the tea processing sector have also adopted woody biomass to run their boilers, while others treat electric poles and fencing/construction posts as well as other timber products.

The negative impacts of selective removal of indigenous tree species for processing and charcoal production have been compounded by overgrazing on the low- lying rangelands in and around the Rift Valley, causing a lot of strain on natural resources, while the medium and high potential agro-ecological zones are under intensive agriculture, forest and nature reserves.

These activities in and around Kenya’s forested areas are encroaching on the rich biodiversity within the forest ecosystem. Past activities and the continued demand for forest products have consequently degraded and decimated Kenya’s forest cover from 20% at Kenya’s independence in 1963, to as low as 2% in the 1990’s.

While immediate restoration efforts have raised forest cover to the current 8.2%, against the 10% UN recommended minimum, and the global convention’s 12.16%, Kenya’s Vision 2030 goal is to meet the more than 4% deficit in forest cover, by 8 planting 360 million trees every year or more, or more than 5 million hectares of additional forest cover to meet the government of Kenya’s stipulated requirement (KFS, 2022).
70% of this forest cover should be as a result of reforestation/afforestation/tree farm planting efforts, while 30% should be due to natural regeneration management as a conservation best practice.

Further, environmental rights and actions are entrenched in the Constitution of Kenya 2010 (Article 42), while the various Acts of Government (including Environmental Management and Coordination Act of 1999) and policy frameworks stipulate the need for pro-active conservation efforts towards attaining the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requirements.

There is tremendous need therefore, to integrate sustainable forest resource development, management and conservation so as to, not only enrich biodiversity, but also to provide a variety of ecosystem goods and services that are essential for domestic use and industrial utilization.

REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a global initiative under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) that aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by preventing deforestation and forest degradation.

It also promotes conservation, sustainable forest management, and enhancement of forest carbon stocks, particularly in developing countries. Key Objectives of REDD+  Reduce emissions from deforestation – Preventing the conversion of forests into agricultural land, urban areas, etc.

 Reduce emissions from forest degradation – Stopping harmful practices like illegal logging and unsustainable fuelwood collection.  Conserve forest carbon stocks – Protecting existing forests to maintain their role as carbon sinks.  Sustainably manage forests – Encouraging responsible logging and forest use.  Enhance forest carbon stocks – Promoting reforestation and afforestation efforts.

How REDD+ Works  Financial Incentives – Countries receive financial rewards for reducing deforestation and maintaining forest cover.  Measurement & Monitoring – Satellite and ground data track forest cover changes and carbon storage.  International Collaboration – Supported by organizations like the UN, World Bank, and NGOs.

 Local Community Involvement – Engages indigenous and local communities in forest ecosystem management. Challenges of REDD+  Governance Issues – Corruption and weak enforcement in some countries.  Land Rights & Indigenous Communities – Ensuring fair benefits for local people.  Funding & Sustainability – Securing long-term financial support.

The organization also contracts for professional fund-raising services to identify and raise funds.

Individual sponsors support 60% of the organization's operating costs, and consistently support the member organizations. Corporate sponsors, civil societies, development agencies and the public sector are critical in mobilizing program grant funds in the future.

MONITORING AND EVALUATION It is anticipated that over 1000 people in each of the 47 counties will participate in the Establishment of 100,000 Tree Nurseries, Seedlings Propagation centers and environmental resource centers and consequently the tree planting exercised dubbed, “expeditions,” and therefore receive valuable information on climate change-related topics designed to increase awareness on biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services management.

Each participant will receive training on how to set up and establish tree nursery and the propagation of tree seedlings. The assessor will determine if residents/participants are responding to the training by correctly planting indigenous and non-invasive species.

A projected 500 residents will then enroll and participate as volunteers for at least three months in a tree watering and nurture exercise program. These individuals will become more aware of conservation through the contact with an instructor trained in forestry and botany as evaluated by a pre- and post-test jointly developed by KFS, KEFRI, TEAMEnvironment KENYA and other stakeholders.

17 All individuals participating in the Expedition will be contacted at least once through phone call, text message, e-mail or mainstream media/social media, to receive environmental conservation information program. Interview surveys will be conducted after the event.

Community surveys will also be administered at the beginning of the project and at the end to measure the impact of the program on community attitudes toward afforestation, reforestation, and agro-forestry and land reclamation.

The Impacts, sustainability and lessons learn from the project will be monitored and reported to enhance the replication of similar events of various scale across the region. Project and facility management best practices shall be employed to document and track progress as well as to benchmark project outcomes towards establishing its impact.

CONCLUSION At the TEAMEnvironment KENYA we are about, “Leaving a HERITAGE for Future Generations of a CLEANER, GREENER (FOOD & WATER SECURE) and a PEACEFUL Environment of Flora, Fauna and Aquatic Life.” This duty, mandate and conservation responsibility cannot be abdicated or delegated to any other but ourselves.
To this course our clarion call is, “Let’s Go Green With You” Best Regards MATHEW OCHANDA EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR. 18 19 20
