content: TEK’S PROPOSAL & COMMITMENT TOWARDS THE TEAMEnvironment KENYA ATTAINMENT OF 30% TREE (FOREST) COVER & ENHANCING CLIMATE RESILIENCE 1/30/2023 TEAMEnvironment KENYA Proposal towards the ATTAINMENT OF 30% TREE (FOREST) COVER & ENHANCING CLIMATE RESILIENCE by 2032. 1 2 .

INTRODUCTION TEAMEnvironment KENYA seeks to plant (Grow) at least One Hundred (100) Million trees and shrubs countrywide, in the above regard we have established a Ten ( 10) Million Tree Nursery and seedlings propagation center at the KAG EAST UNIVERSITY in Kajiado County which has 165,000 assorted tree species of seedlings ready for planting.

The Tree Nurseries and seedlings propagation centers are to be replicated in the rest of the 46 counties. We look forward to do this through our initiative dubbed SERP, “SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION PROGRAMME.” This is in response to the Decree by the President H.E Dr.

William Samoei Ruto on Mashujaa day 20th OCTOBER 2022 and government’s commitment to increase the Tree (Forest) Cover to more than 30% by 2032. Grow five (5) Billion Trees for the next 5 years and additional 10Billion by 2032. Secure, rehabilitate and protect public forests. Rehabilitate, restore all degraded water towers an d other forest ecosystems.

This will significantly c ontribute to the fight against desertification and CLIMATE CHANGE and therefore bring about the realization of a, “GREEN ECONOMY ” which is anchored on the BIG FOUR Government’s Agenda.

This new target pro vides a challenge a nd an employment opportunity to millions of youth and women groups countrywide as they work towards improving the environment by engaging in agribusiness and agroforestry farming practice. This entails massive seedlings propagation, nurturing and growing of the trees whose demand is now at 360 Million seedlings per year.

TEK has been on the front row championing and spearhead the GREENING KENYA INITIAVE & Conservation Mission consistently for the last five (5) years now across the country and have planted at least 2.5 Million Trees in various counties the furthest being Wajir county where with the support of the county government we conducted a Ten (10) thousand tree planting (growing) expedition in the month of October 2019 TEAMEnvironment KENYA has a commitment and determination towards reclamation of degraded landscape and forest resources for the good of humanity and the ecosystems through adventure and sporting activities dubbed, “Expeditions” which involves activities such as , mountain climbing, cycling & skating and running (marathon) in the 47 Counties as we propagate the message of peace and encourage (peaceful coexistence amongst communities) social cohesion and introgression in our county and countrywide conservation initiatives.
This process will improve productivity of the degraded forest lands , improve food security, reduces poverty, enhances climate change , resilience, adaptation and fosters sustainable development.

This exercise presents many new challenges and opportunities in the efforts to conserve soil, our water towers, biodiversity, restore ecological services and facilitate human well-being in and around deforested or degraded forest landscapes.
The tremendous material and human resource requirements, as well as the technical and financial pre -requisites call for cross -sector and multi - stakeholder approach and inclusion.

3 In our quest and desire to bring change and transformation in our environmen t and ecosystem countrywide TEAMEnvironment Kenya i s working in partnership and collaboration with the var ious County Governments and other agencies/organizations at the county level, business communities, schools/institutions and all stakeho lders so as to ensure a successful execution and consequent realization of the Ten ( 10) Million Trees planting (growing) target by 2025 in our endeavor to realizing the desired 10% Tree (Forest) Cover.

To realize the above and desired target TEAMEnvironment Kenya is engaging its members who comprises of Youth and Women in various parts of the 47 counties to establish Tre e Nurseries and seedlings propagation centers with the hope and aim of having a One (1) Million Tree Nursery in each of the 47 counties .
The seedlings will be of assorted species which will include - Fruit Trees (various kind), Indigenous Tress, Exotic Trees and Bamboo.

4 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY TEAMEnvironment KENYA is a Non -Governmental Environmental Association which constitutes of youth and women organizations, schools, institutions of higher learning, community members and other institutions who are focused on Greening and Environmental Conservation as a means to reversing the challenges of global warming and climate change.

Our philosophy of, “Leaving a Heritage for Future Generations” underscores the mandate, duty and responsibility to make (and be) the desired change towards green lifestyles in an endeavor to address ourselves to environmental challenges and various components of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This will ensure green and clean homes, workplaces, communities, towns, counties, countries and to ultimate ly find lasting solutions for our ‘environments’ towards a habitable “planet Earth” now and for posterity. TEK is a cross-sector and multi-stakeholder forum consisting of ecosystem conservation enthusiasts and ecosystem services experts.

Our collaborative framework and devoted team of environmental and forestry professionals as well as community development expert s has enabled us to design and is helping us implement on inclusive and sustainable programs which offer solutions by rendering biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services management with community -level sustainable development in mind.

Our liaison w ith the county government(s), private sector, civil society, youth and women groups (TEK Members) , development agencies and academia actors with the inclusive involvement of community members/their organizations or groups gives basis to our various program s.

The Tree Nursery establishments, Seedlings Propa gation centers, Environmental Resource Development and subsequent Tree Planting (Growing) Expeditions in the 47 counties will be our repeatable model in cognizance of various ecological zones and both the fruit trees, indigenous and non -invasive exotic tree species of medicinal, cultural, nutritional, ornamental, woody biomass and/or ecological significance.

TEK has a huge representation of at least 700 registered members in the 47 counties who are always ready and willing to volunteer and travel to the respective counties to be part of the adventurous expedition where they collectively roll-up of their sleeves to doing their #LittleThing of doing good to Mother Nature, the environment by conserving, restoring, rehabilitating and protecting humanities lifeblood/line which is our biodiversity.
With your partnership and support TEK will work on projects that will mobilize youth, women and community volunteers to establish 1,000,000 tree nurseries in the 47 Counties.

These tree nurseries will be established in schools, institutions, public and private farm lands in the various wards and sub counties, they are to be managed by the youth and women groups in these locations against and MOU and Partnership deed that will be signed with this entities and institutions.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA is engaged at the grass root and community level to sensitize and mobilize local groups with several smallholder households, youth & women groups, community forest associations, other CBOs, schools, social enterprises inclusively engaged.
The expected annual successful propagation of 10,000 seedlings per nursery from the anticipated 50,000 nurseries all across the country in the 47 counties will exceed 500 million seedlings per ye ar.

The nurseries will be established with the professional guidance and technical support of KFS and KEFRI extension service officers with supervision and technical assistance by TEK in liaison with its volunteers to rehabilitate and restore our riparian areas, Wetlands and the Water Towers (gazette and yet -to-be gazetted) in liaison with respective national and county government agencies.

TEK will then establish facility management best practices on the nursery resource and seedlings propagation centers with sound monitoring, evaluation and reporting mechanisms to ensure program sustainability and its consequent success.

5 TEAMEnvironment KENYA over the years has aggressively been involved in Environmental education, Awareness creation, sensitization and mobilization of communities to plant and nurture the trees though agro-forestry, farm woodlot development, community forest restoration, water towers (catchment) reclamation and conservation, dry land forestry and nutritional/medicinal plantation forestry.

TEK will collaborate with KFS, KEFRI and other environmental agencies at the county level in running extensive sensitization campaigns. We shall intensify our efforts in the above regard in sourcing and sorting of species of tree seedlings, assist in preparing the ground, plant and nurture the seedlings and monitor their progress with the right feedback systems.

The resource restoration program will accommodate various land-use practices, including agriculture, agro-forestry, wildlife conservation, forest regeneration management, contract farm plantations, and riparian lands as well as coastal forest management and conservation.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA works in collaboration with KFS, KEFRI and other environmental agencies, aims to inculcate tree planting (growing) culture/habit to anyone and everyone and people of all ages, reforestation, agro -forestry, and other greening best environmental practices that enhance conservation, restoration and biodiversity protection at community level, county level, nationwide and across the continent; thereby contributing to the legacy of a green heritage, a habitable, peaceful, and clean environment for all, now and in posterity.

Vision To be the most resourceful national network of cross -sector and multi -stakeholder a ctors committed to creating a GREEN LEGACY in the conservation and protection of biodiversity and ecosystem services by the restoration , rehabilitation and nurture of our fragile flora, fauna and aquatic life.

Mission To foster climate change adaptation and mitigation by develop ing community resilience interventions for enhanced local knowledge, well-being, asset building, green value -chains and sustainable development.

Core Values The core guiding principles for the achievement of the TEK Mission are in dividual and organizational virtues including the following among many others:  Integrity: Is our bed rock. A ll engagements are based on honesty, transparency and accountability.

 Inclusivity: An all -hands-on-deck model of participatory involvement of primar y and secondary stakeholders in sustainable development.  Environmental Responsibility : individual and shared responsibility, to reduce the environmental carbon footprint through established ecological goals, and in following through on environmental commitments.

6  Commitment to Green Legacy: To inspire community level adoption of green lifestyles and integrating environmental best practices into sustainable activities that conserve biodiversity and help secure ecosystem services for the future as a legacy and heritage for posterity.
 Livelihood Support : commitment to enhancing the safety, health and well -being of the members by implementing solution -oriented activities in their communities’ places of stay and work.

Strategic Objectives  Stakeholder Sensitization and Mobilization: Initiating promotional and advocacy campaigns to sensitize stakeholders and empower their initiative to act in preparation and response to climate change. Creating networking opportunities and linkages among stakeholders.

 Scaling up cap acity: Organizing training workshops and meetings to establish and facilitate an effective training program for trainers, mentor’s/opinion shapers and leaders of change. Offering consultancy services in greening to d evelop and equip communities with tools that they need for homegrown initiatives in mitigating and adapting to climate change.

 Change Management: Inspire, embrace and initiate change among stakeholders in shifting the paradigm to encourage and adopt green best practices. Encouraging effective u se of climate-smart technologies and by engaging communities to embrace conservation and sustainable natural resource utilization. Undertaking environmental conservation and ecosystem protection activities.

 Conflict Resolution: Establish an effective monit oring, resolution and reporting human - wildlife conflicts and a digital application system for feed -back in addressing matters arising from human interactions with fellow humans as well as with wildlife and natural resources.

 Disaster Preparedness and Mitig ation: Proactive information sharing and early advisory systems on environmental challenges as well as mobilization of support actions by members. Sharing relevant information and assistance for livelihood enhancement.

 Formalization: Registration, documentation and legalization , as well as linkaging, mainstreaming and business development support for TEK member operations.  Resource Mobilization and Fund Raising: We are working towards employing solid resource mobilization strategies which will ensur e a successful implementation of the Tree Nursery Establishment and Seedlings Propagation initiatives.

Engaging in resource mobilization and fundraising for conservation and livelihood causes through the e stablishment of an impact investing and asset buil ding platform for smallholder households and stakeholder program activities.

 Social Entrepreneurship: Develop green value-chains by engaging in business for change and sustainable/green enterprise with an aim of benefiting base of the pyramid households an d micro-enterprises.

 Lobby: Making recommendations to and lobbies policy makers on climate change issues on a platform mounted to voice concerns on environmental degradation, deforestation and 7 community marginalization, and as well to lobby the county government(s) and other relevant stakeholders in biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services management. STATEMENT OF NEED Kenya is 80% ASALs.

Notwithstanding, the ASALs and the remaining 20% high potential areas are under tremendous pressure from inc reasing demand for natural forest resources as raw materials, alternative land -use, infrastructural developmental activities, and challenges related to poverty.

While forests are an important environmental resource and play a valuable role in not only the balance of ecosystems as a habitat for critical flora , fauna and aquatic life. T hey enhance the livelihoods of people in communities across the country, the region and beyond.

There is a gap however, between ecosystem services; that largely remain in the corridors of professional deliberations, consultations and amendments; and the elaborate and direct involvement of communities’/sector actors in adopting and engaging in the act ivities necessary to enhance these ecosystem services and foster attendant socio -economic and environmental benefits which TEAMEnvironment seeks to cover and this, “the Establishment of 1,000,000 Tree Nurseries & Seedlings Propagation centers and environmental resource centers in each of the 47 counties.

Kenya consumes about 80 million trees per year, causing a need for 450 million trees annually for the forest resource requirements to be sustainably met. This is due to Kenya’s heavy dependence on biomass energy, deforestation and forest degradation.

The degradation may be due to forest fires , which we have had rampant happenings of in the resent past which adversely affected our Main WATER TOWERS; Mount Kenya, Mau Forest and Abadares Ranges respectively.

T his was due to the outstretched drought season and unsustainable charcoal production, poor agricultural expansion activity, overgrazing, poorly planned settlements, excessive extraction of forest resources, or over - cultivation.

Notably, charcoal and firewood account for about 70% of primary energy consumption, and d espite the government’s recent ban on illegal logging and extraction of forest products , the demand for timber has gone up due to its scarcity and consequent its price. Biomass energy is still high and rising due to poverty levels, population growth and urbanization.

The biggest incentives to unsustainable charcoal production are also the greatest disincentives to all environmental conservation and ecosystem protection efforts: the annual retail value of the industry is currently estimated betwee n KES 40 to 80 billion (USD 400 –800 million) according to the KFS reports.

The charcoal business has continued to thrive, yet it is illegal since no registration has been made for a single charcoal producer association because corruption drives this huge so called ‘black market’ enterprise.

Manufacturers, especially in the tea processing sector have also adopted woody biomass to run their boilers, while others treat electric poles and fencing/construction posts as well as other timber products.

The negative impacts of selective removal of indigenous tree species for processing and charcoal production have been compounded by overgrazing on the low -lying rangelands in and around the Rift Valley, causing a lot of strain on natural resources, while the medium and high potential agro -ecological zones are under intensive agriculture, forest and nature reserves.

These activities in and around Kenya’s forested areas are encroaching on the rich biodiversity within the forest ecosystem. Past activities and the continued demand for forest products have consequently degraded and decimated Kenya’s forest cover from 20% at Kenya’s independence in 1963 , to as low as 2% in the 1990’s.

While immediate restoration efforts have raised forest cover to the current 7.2%, against the 10% UN recommended minimum, and the global convention’s 12.16%, Kenya’s Vision 2030 goal is to meet the more than 4% deficit in f orest cover, by planting 360 million trees every year or more, or 8 more than 5 million hectares of additional forest cover to meet the government of Kenya’s stipulated requirement (KFS, 2022).
70% of this forest cover should be as a result of reforestation/afforestation/tree farm planting efforts, while 30% should be due to natural regeneration management as a conservation best practice.

Further, environmental rights and actions are entrenched in the Constitution of Kenya 2010 (Article 42), whi le the various Acts of Government (including Environmental Management and Coordination Act of 1999) and policy frameworks stipulate the need for pro -active conservation efforts towards attaining the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requirements.

There is tremendous need therefore, to integrate sustainable forest resource development, management and conservation so as to, not only enrich biodiversity, but also to provide a variety of ecosystem goods and services that are essential for domestic use and industrial utilization.

The NATIONAL Government of Kenya’s Relevance to the Project As TEAMEnvironment KENYA we offer ourselves as the most ideal and strategic partners to support the National government to conduct environmental restoration and rehabilitation initiatives to help in its ambitious yet doable plan to significantly increasing forest cover to at least 10% by 2025.

A total ban on logging and utilization of forests and its products was imposed early this year 2018 and a moratorium imposed on all forest products all in an effort to protect our forests and the natural resources, restore river basins, water catchments and our water towers.

The initiative and program is intended to contribute to the glob al fight against climate change, global warming and to build and enhance resilience through conservation of biodiversity, protection of water sources and catchments, conservation of soil, and scaling of environmental assets.

This informs the Government of Kenya’s commitment to restoring 5.1 million hectares of forests in the country through the Ministry of Environment and Forestry with the objectives of achieving:-  The global goals to climate change, mitigation, adaptation and enhance resilience.

 The constitutional mandate of Kenya to maintain at least 10% of national forest cover,  The Kenya`s vision 2030 of rehabilitating and protecting Kenya`s water towers in order to increase, regulate and maintain high quality water flowing from this catchments, and  The National Climate Change Response Strategy`s goal of growing 7.6 billion trees and shrubs for ecological restoration and sustainable land management, to be coordinated by Kenya Forest Service with technical support from Clinton Climate Initiative and the World Resource Centre.

This commitment is to be attained through partnerships and collaborations with TEAMEnvironment KENYA. The REDD+ Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) Initiative mooted in September, 2014 and coordinated by the Kenya Forest Service with technical support from Clinton Cli mate Initiative and the World Resource Centre.

The National Restoration strategy is has a technological framework that synergizes environmental restoration information with government and r elevant actors, including the private sector, civil society, communities and development partners among others. It also serves as a structured method for identifying key success factors for existing and lacking forest landscape restoration opportunities.

9 TEAMEnvironment KENYA’s Shared Values Environmental restoration is as critical in rural areas, as it is in urban ecosystems. Urban rivers are under pressure from effluent pollution, sub -catchments are being encroached on, and vegetation cover is under thr eat of degradation, while waste management remains a tremendous challenge. There also is the problem of air and noise pollution.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA will catalyze action by cross-sector multi -stakeholders through participatory communication and joint facilitation. TEK’s community inclusion structure and information sharing practice strengthens the links towards the effective enhancement of wealth, well-being and dignified living among smallholder households to attain sustainable development goals.

The TEK professional team is transparent in the ir pragmatic delivery of catalytic interventions for triple bottom-line impact. Public education and awareness creation is a core component in our programs, initiatives and planned activities. Our goal therefore w ill be to enhance local knowledge and scale capacity for adoption of interventions and sharing of indigenous knowledge.

The programs will involve school students, whom we shall be seeking to inculcate conservation and environmental restoration practices, and stimulate the early adoption of green -value chain development actions. TEK works with institutions of hig her learning to engage volunteers and professionals in the multi -stakeholder conservation and restoration programs.

The development and dissemination of climate information and early warning s igns systems is part of awareness creation among the public and the stakeholders. It is essential to prevent disasters and/or respond proactively so as to reduce the extent of their effect to communities.

TEK will also collaborate with other environmental & conservation stakeholders to mount policy platforms and voice matters of ecological consequence for substantive action by the relevant authorities. TEAMEnvironment KENYA’s Liaison Proposition Partnership and collaboration is critical to ensure the success of the project.

T EAMEnvironment KENYA therefore will strategically collaborates through an MOU with other environmental partners and conservation stakeholders operating in the following sectors among others :- Agriculture, Agribusiness, agro -forestry and Agro -industry; Environment; Water and Sanitation ; Eco-tourism; Construction and (Green Building Services ); Transport (Green Mobility); Renewable Energy (Wind, Water and S olar) and Energy Efficiency ; Health; Disaster Preparedness; Finance; Policy formulation and Regulatory; Training, Learning and Capacity Development ; Academia and Media (Production of environmental and conservation content).
However, as per the TEK governan ce structure, the mainstreaming of member activities is critical during the interpretation of the stakeholder MoUs.

Therefore, any Joint ventures, (Public private community partnership) PPCPs or any other contractual agreements negotiated by TEK on behalf of member entities for products and/or services that they render on the projects, aside from the volunteerism aspects, are deemed legally binding in regard to set terms of agreement.

TEK’s Proposed Mandate as Partner TEAMEnvironment KENYA is a duty -bound c limate change resiliency and sustainable development forum whose strategy entails sensitization, mobilization and implementation on greening and environmental stewardship.

TEK engages in advocacy and capacity building activities, eco - stewardship, as well a s training in the adoption by communities of eco -friendly lifestyles and climate-smart resource utilization for social, economic and environmental sustainability.

10 The day-to-day activities will be facilitated by TEK’s volunteers and fiduciary staff whose expertise will be employed to offer an advisory and coordination role and guide the proper functioning of the joint initiative to meet the set out objectives.

Stakeholder meetings and conventions will set up of the agenda of existing and new projects in line with the criteria and values set out on the Memorandum of Understanding. The overall mandate is to:  Take into account local content, the local context and indigenous knowledge in order to sustainably integrate local skills and resources.  Oversee the implementation of the project.

 Conduct capacity building and offer technical support to the community members.  Offer oversight, management and development support to the community member activities.  Conduct Monitoring, evaluation and reporting activities and offer general facility management on the project.

TEAMEnvironment KENYA’s Commitment to the Proposed Mandate This mandate provides TEK members with opportunities to learn from each other’s experience and to benefit from the advantages of a resourceful network of organizations towards the realization of the TEK Vision and Strategic Plan.

TEK extensively undertakes strategic partnership a ctions for impact in climate change , adaptation, mitigation to see how we can build and enhance resilience on the premise of the comprehensive legislative and policy frameworks available on biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services.

TEK forges Joint efforts or public-private and community partnership (ppcp) platforms to address the pertinent issues and choices, an d effectively roll -out programs of activities for implementation on the basis of recommended best practices and according to set benchmarks of actualization.

TEK’s key stakeholders focus on emerging opportunities while analyzing innovative options available in addressing the various challenges faced, meeting the expectations and drawing lessons learnt for continuous growth and development. TEAMEnvironment KENYA plans, prioritizes develops and im plements on innovative programs and projects that meet the criteria for greening objectives.

The Establishment of 1,000,000 Tree Nurseries & Seedlings Propagation centers and environmental resource centers in each of the 47 counties, Agro-forestry, forest conservation and natural resource management are climate -smart landscape development best practices that TEK engages in to enhance food secu rity, sustain the livelihoods of indigenous/local communities and smallholder households, create biological diversity, sustain habitat for wildlife, carbon sequesterization (sinks), climatic change mitigation and adoption, and to contribute towards Kenya’s attainment of the global agenda, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

TEK will engage key stakeholders directly to sensitize and build capacity for attitude change to adopting and embracing blue collar jobs, agribusiness and agroforestry business ven tures by youths, while highlighting the incentives of the program and its activities. Stakeholder-inclusive mapping out of landscapes identifies requirements for reclamation and restoration from a community stand point.

This underpins the thematic approach es in implementing remedial programs and activities (events and projects). 11 TEKs focus on priority areas for restoration includes degraded are as, natural forests with below 10% cover, national parks and game reserves, private natural forests, forest farms/woodlots, and dry lands in accordance to participatory forest and natural resource management plans.

ACTIVITIES AND GOALS TO MEET THE STRATEGIC OBJECTIVES  Stakeholder Sensitization and Mobilization: During the launch of the Tree Nurseries, Seedlings Propagation centers and environmental resource centers w e shall have branded T-shirts, caps, Banners, Posters, Tear Drops, wrist bands and other promotional materials are utilized during sensitization campaigns while social and mainstream media are employ ed to stimulate action by stakeholders in the various capacities.
 Scaling up capacity: We shall have an Eco-tourism component to enhance community immersion by external stakeholder while local knowledge is shared and lessons learnt.

TEK will establish tree nurseries in liaison with community members as a community asset, resource center and contact point for external stakeholders to visit and experience sights and sounds of community’s cultural, biodiversity and historical significance.

 Change Management: The use of ICT and appropriate technologies and innovations including aquaponics, organic agriculture, mushroom farming, horticulture, drip irrigation, rain water harvesting, upstream processing of raw materials, alternative livestock (bee - keeping, exotic and indigenous poultry, butterflies, silk worms, paddock and zero grazing, cooperative development, contract agribusiness, impact investing among others.

 Conflict Resolution: Stakeholder liaison to develop GPS system and mobile application tool s to monitor trends in climate change an d the progress of mitigation, adaptation and building resilience efforts, in order to pre -empt crises and conflicts pertaining to migration patterns, deficiencies in food/fodder supplies and any possible conflict poi nts and offer essential mitigation support services.

 Disaster Preparedness, Mitigation and building Resilience : The Kenya Meteorological department and stakeholder GPS technology are used to inform the general public of impending disasters while social and mainstream media outlets disseminate this information to enhance disaster preparedness.  Resource Mobilization and Fund Raising: Utilize of promotional materials ie.

Organization T- shirts, caps, hoodies, wrist bands , registration of members during confere nces, corporate sponsorships, event proceeds, tree seedling sales, facility management concession agreements and other income generating activities to raise funds while generating competent funding proposals to source for grants and funds.

 Social Entrepre neurship: Green-value chains around organic agriculture, fair trade, sustainably produced forest products including bio -char, bamboo products, bio -fuel, poles, posts, timber, furniture among other products and services rendered by members.
12  Lobby: Convening and participating in round table meetings with policy formulators and other stakeholders to deliberate on pertinent environmental issues and facilitation of our activities.

TEK Envisioned Members and Stakeholders/Beneficiaries of the Project  Ordinary members include community level individuals, smallholder household enterprises, community members/general public, CBO’s, and community level micro -entrepreneurs, youth/students and youth organizations, youth -led enterprises, women -led enterprises, volunteers among others.

The members directly or indirectly benefit from various initiatives, activities and events. Youth -based institutions (such as schools and other learning/training institutions) also are affiliate but on a different collaborative framework w hose structure allows them to adopt a tree and let students benefit from green value-chains for school fees, shopping and pocket money.

 Affiliate members shall be drawn from several organizational stakeholders both in private and public sector. Affiliate m embers shall actually be partners and shall be classified into Platinum, Gold, Silver and Bronze depending on specified levels of collaboration and sponsorship.

The Partnership will mobilize the affiliate members to raise funds and offer various technical and financial inputs as corporate entities (through their CSR components and/or Foundations), National Government ministries/ agencies, County Government Institutions, the academia, the media fraternity among others.

 Development agencies and Civil Society Organizations as important partners in the realization of the Partnership’s thematic approach to sustainable development with inclusivity for community level actors will linkage primary stakeholders’ efforts towards socio-economic and environmental sustainability.

PROGRAMME DEVELOPMENT PROCESS Phase 1: The intensive processes of identifying locations, schools, institutions, public and private homes and places for establishing the nurseries with water and security guarantee.

Where we shall sort the indigenous , exotic and non -invasive species of trees that suit cultural, ornamental, nutritional, and medicinal as well as conservation/restoration functi ons as guided by the ecological zones and tree planting (growing) will be guided by the KFS and KEFRI.

After the seedling will have matured and ready for planting, TEAMEnvironment KENYA will make arrangements on the logistics and delivering of the seedlings to the various planting sites b efore the commencement of the Tree Planting (growing) Exercise.

Before that there will have been an sensitization and mobilization of volunteers, community members and the general public to participate in the Expedition and the tree planting (growing) exercise as it will be happening in their wards and villages and hopefully have transport arrangements made for as many volunteers as we would be interested in participating in the exercise facilitated as this will ensure ownership of the activity and consequently its success.

Phase 2: Providing of meal, transport and a ccommodation to volunteer delegates that will be part of the initiative and therefore facilitate them to be undertake the county and countrywide massive tree planting (growing) exercise in the respective planting locations in the various counties all around the country for the period, including providing them with emergency services if it shall be needed.

13 Phase 3: Submission of Forest F acility Management Proposals :- At the end of the project, TEK will institute a facility management proposal and engage local community members/groups in nurturing the young seedlings to maturity. A 1 MILLION TREE NURSERY will be established in the 47 counties across the country will scale up the expansion of forests further.

This will integrate the Expedition initiative that is to be conducted under the SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENT RESTORATION PROGRAM (SERP) by TEK. This will help to build resilience to climate change and the adaptive capacity of communities in respective counties and around the country.

The proposal will highlight key components on the region, communities, project implementation through participatory forest management planning, outcomes and partnering stakeholders in project execution. County government as custodian of community forest s hall also award a KFS -structured participatory forest management plan on the project.

Phase 4: Tree Nursery Establishment, Seedlings Propagation and Resource Centre Development :- Various tree nurseries in various regions of the county and a country in the need to scale capacity for a large variety of trees, shrubs, grass and other plants with functions including conservation, carbon sink, biomass, medicinal, cultural, nutritional/ fruit, fodder, building, energy/fuel/firewood, shade, and ornamental.

The project will focus on keeping stocks of indigenous trees and exotic non-invasive species, and using local resources to develop tree nurseries to lower operation expenses and reduce prices. The project professionals will ensure there is sufficient tree nurs ery capacity with good quality seedlings.

All participants Youths, Women and any other interested persons will be trained on best methods of tree nursery establishment and development, tree planting and nurture for trees for optimal growth and productivity.

OTHER POTENTIAL ACTIVITIES Eco-Camp: The development of Eco-Camp by extension will provide TEK as stop overs and parking places as they traverse the counties with their conservation initiative giving them an Eco-Tourism Expeditions Experience.

At this site we can have periodic health screening services offered as part of the event, including blood test s, blood pressure screeni ngs, and lifestyle issues screening ( high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and sedentary lifestyle). Health, Safety and Environmental Program: The disaster management training progra m could include instructors to each lead a periodic class training on basic life skills such as: -emergency evacuation, firefighting to help in (forests and wild fires) , floods and other environmental disaster preparedness, occupational safety, wild animal hazards, and health to community members .

The instructor will also p rovide information on other issues and answer related questions from participants. Swimming and Exercise Program: Exercise instructors will each lead a daily thirty-minute class on swimming and health exercise at our Environmental Hub and Resource Center.

The instructor will 14 also provide information on fitness, cardiovascular health, and diet, and answer health -related questions from participants. This will not only improve the health o f tourists who visit the area, but also locals while raising funds for community benefit activities.

Follow-up/Outreach: The replicable model of this project shall be strengthened by lessons learnt at community level and reported on the comprehensive monit oring and evaluation strategy. The scaling of project activities and the partnership’s entry into other geographies is essential for shared objectives and competencies.

The ‘Big Box’: pre-emptive philanthropy is part of the triple bottom-line activities undertaken by TEK at the base of the pyramid. Food and livelihood supplies to community’s abjectly poor can be distributed once s ourced on TEK’ Big Box Program , where volunteers collect household and other items not required anymore and coordinate to the warehouse for distribution.

Strategic Innovation: The partnership’s strategists will consistently review the potential for innovative project activities that are of triple bottom -line impact and present the draft concepts for review and approval and concomi tant implementation .

A term strategic plan shall be drafted to comprehensively define the objectives, goals, inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, impacts and lessons learnt for improvement. The timelines , other participating stakeholders and costs shall also be defined.

LONG-TERM SOURCES/STRATEGIES FOR FUNDING TEAMEnvironment KENYA will come up with resource mobilization and fund raising strategy for sponsorship on various programs, and has sustained program strategy for resource mobilization and revenue creating engagements on the social enterprise platforms.

The Impacts, sustainability and lessons learn from the project will be monitored and reported to enhance the replication of similar events of various scale across the region. Project and facility management best practices shall be employed to document and track progress as well as to benchmark project outcomes towards establishing its impact.

INTRODUCTION TEAMEnviroment KENY A is a Socio-Economic, Humanitarian Non-governmental Environmental Organization (National Environment and Conservation Movement). The trend setters in conservation on our mission to keep Kenya, Clean, Green and breathing.

Championing the 15 Billlion T ree Growing Agenda. Our T en (10) Million T ree Nursery, Seedling Propagation and Study Center is at the Kabarak University in Nakuru County currently housing 350,000 assorted seedlings ready for planting. We plan to replicate these tree nurseries across the 46 counties through our "SUST AINABLE ENVIRONMENT AL RESTORA TION PROGRAMME" (SERP).

This initiative directly supports President H.E. Dr . William Samoei Ruto's directive on Mashujaa Day, October 20th 2022, and the government's commitment to increase national tree and forest cover to 30% by 2032. This is by growing 15 billion trees by 2032, alongside efforts to secure, rehabilitate, and protect public forests and restore degraded water towers and other forest ecosystems.

Our efforts will significantly help in combating , desertification and climate change; fostering a "GREEN ECONOMY" . This is inline with the government's Climate Action; 15 Billion T ree Growing Agenda. This ambitious target creates substantial employment opportunity for millions of youth and women groups nationwide.

By engaging in agribusiness and agroforestry, they will enhance environmental restoration through massive seedlings propagation, nurturing, and tree growing thereby addressing the current demand of 360 million seedlings per year .

Our Conservation Mission and T rack Record TEAMEnvironment KENY A has consistently championed the Greening Kenya Initiative through its nationwide conservation mission for the past six years. During this period, we successfully planted (grown) over 2.8 million trees across the country in different counties.

A notable achievement includes 10,000-tree planting (growing) expeditions which we conducted in the North Eastern Counties, they include Wajir , Marsabit, Garisa and Isiolo counties where we planted a total of 100,000+ seedlings between 2019 and 2021. This we conducted with the support of the community and the respective county governments.

TEK is committed to reclaiming and rehabilitating degraded landscapes and restoring vital forest resources, benefiting both human and local ecosystems. We achieved this through unique adventure and sporting "Expeditions" across the 47 counties, featuring activities such as mountain climbing, cycling & skating for Climate action and marathon.

These initiatives not only advance environmental conservations but also promote peace, foster social cohesion amongest communities and strengthens co-existence in our national conservation efforts. Our Approach to Climate Action and Environmental Restoration.

Reclaiming Degradable Lands We restore degradable forest lands to improve productivity, enhance food security, reduce povety, conserve soils, protect water towers, and boost biodiversity for human well being. Building Climate Resilience Our initiatives strengthens climate change resilience and adaptation, fostering sustainable development by restoring ecological balance in defforested landscapes.

Multistake Holder Collaborations TEAMEnvironment KENY A patners with the National and County governments environmental agencies they include; KFS, NEMA, KEFRI, KWS. This collaborative effort aims to plant (grow) 100,000,000 trees by 2032, supporting government in achieving 30% national tree and forest cover .

Community Lead Nursery By engaging youth and women groups in the 47 counties,with an aim of establishing a 1 million tree seedlings nursery per county. This nurseries will have assorted seedlings species. Which will include fruit trees indegenious trees, exotic trees and bamboo.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY TEAMEnvironment KENY A is a socio economic, non-governmental environmental membership organization that constitute youth and women organizations, schools & institutions, community members, and other diverse groups. We are dedicated to environmental conservation and greening initiatives, actively combating climate change and mitigating the effects of global warming.

Our philosophy, "Leaving a Heritage for Future Generations, " underscores our unwavering commitment to fostering sustainable lifestyles, effectively addressing environmental challenges, and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This dedication drives our efforts to promote green and clean environments across homes, workplaces, communities, towns, counties, and countries, ensuring a habitable 'Planet Earth' for all generations. TEK serves as a cross-sectoral, multi-stakeholder forum, convening ecosystem conservationists and experts in ecosystem services.

It is supported by a dedicated team of environmental, forestry, and community development professionals, this collaborative framework enables the design and implementation of inclusive and sustainable programs. These programs deliver solutions by integrating biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services management with sustainable community development.

Our programs are built on strong partnerships with county governments, the private sector , civil society, TEK Members (youth and women groups), development agencies, and academic institutions, alongside the inclusive involvement of community members.

A key repeatable model involves establishing T ree Nurseries and Seedling Propagation Centers, followed by T ree Planting (Growing) Expeditions across all 47 counties. This model considers various ecological zones and prioritizes fruit trees, indigenous species, and non-invasive exotic trees with medicinal, cultural, nutritional, ornamental, woody biomass, or ecological significance.

Our 10,000,000 T ree Million Seedlings Initiative. TEAMEnvironment KENY A (TEK) mobilizes an extensive network of over 700 registered members across the 47 counties. These dedicated volunteers are committed to preserving, restoring, and protecting biodiversity4a vital resource for humanity.

With your partnership and support, TEK will seeks establish 1,000,000 tree nurseries throughout the rest of 46 counties, engaging youth, women, and community volunteers in this critical effort. These nurseries will be established in schools, institutions, and on public and private farmlands within various wards and sub-counties.

Local youth and women groups will manage them under a signed Memorandum of Understanding (MOUs) and partnership agreements with the respective entities and institutions. TEK actively engages grassroots communities, sensitizing and mobilizing local groups including smallholder households, youth and women groups, community forest associations, CBOs, schools, and social enterprises.

This initiative projects the annual propagation of 10,000 seedlings per nursery from the 50,000 nurseries across the 47 counties, producing over 500 million seedlings per year. Nurseries will receive professional guidance and technical support from KFS and KEFRI extension service officers, with additional supervision and technical assistance provided by TEK and its volunteers.
This initiative aims to rehabilitate and restore riparian areas, wetlands, and gazetted (and yet-to-be-gazetted) Water T owers, collaborating with relevant national and county government agencies.

TEK will ensure best practices for facility management at these nursery resource and seedling propagation centers, incorporating robust monitoring, evaluation, and reporting mechanisms to guarantee program sustainability and success. Vision, Mission & Core Values Vision T o be the premier national network of cross-sector stakeholders, dedicated to forging a lasting green legacy.

We achieve this by conserving, protecting, restoring, rehabilitating and nurturing our vital biodiversity and its essential ecosystem services. Mission T o advance climate change adaptation and mitigation through powerful community resilience initiatives.

These initiatives enhance local knowledge, improve well-being, build sustainable assets, promote green value chains, and drive comprehensive sustainable development. Core Values Our core values define TEK's mission, embodying the individual and organizational principles that guide our work: Integrity Integrity is our foundation.

All engagements are built on honesty, transparency, and accountability. Inclusivity We embrace a participatory model, actively involving all primary and secondary stakeholders to drive sustainable development.

Environmental Responsibility We champion individual and collective responsibility to reduce our environmental footprint, adhering to established ecological goals and unwavering environmental pledges. Commitment to Green Legacy We inspire community-level adoption of green lifestyles and integrate environmental best practices into sustainable activities.

Our goal is to conserve biodiversity and secure ecosystem services for future generations. Livelihood Support We enhance the safety, health, and well-being of our members by implementing solution-oriented activities within their communities and workplaces.

Strategic Objectives & Activities Stakeholder Engagement & Mobilization Launch advocacy and awareness campaigns to empower stakeholders for proactive climate change preparation and response. Foster networking and establish critical linkages among all relevant parties. Capacity Building Develop and deliver effective training programs for trainers, mentors, and change leaders.

Provide specialized greening consultancy services to equip communities with essential tools for localized climate mitigation and adaptation solutions. Driving T ransformative Change Inspire a paradigm shift among stakeholders to embrace green best practices.

Promote climate-smart technologies and engage communities in sustainable natural resource management, enhancing environmental conservation and ecosystem protection. Conflict Resolution & Monitoring Implement effective systems for monitoring, resolving, and reporting human-wildlife conflicts. Develop a digital application for feedback on interactions among humans, wildlife, and natural resources.

Disaster Preparedness & Mitigation Facilitate proactive information sharing and early warning systems for environmental challenges. Mobilize member support and provide livelihood assistance to enhance community disaster preparedness. Operational Formalization Support the registration, documentation, and legalization of TEK member operations.

Facilitate their integration, mainstreaming, and provide business development support to strengthen organizational foundation and impact. Resource Mobilization & Fundraising Implement robust resource mobilization strategies to ensure successful T ree Nursery Establishment and Seedlings Propagation initiatives.

Actively fundraise for conservation and livelihood causes by establishing an impact investing and asset- building platform for smallholder households and stakeholder programs. Promoting Social Entrepreneurship Develop sustainable green value chains by fostering businesses that drive change.

Support sustainable enterprises to benefit households at the base of the pyramid and micro-enterprises, creating positive social and environmental impact. Advocacy & Lobbying Formulate recommendations and lobby policymakers on critical climate change issues. Utilize a dedicated platform to voice concerns regarding environmental degradation, deforestation, and community marginalization.

Actively engage with national, county governments and other stakeholders to advocate for biodiversity conservation and effective ecosystem services management. ST A TEMENT OF NEED & Kenya's Forest Challenge With 80% of its land comprising Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs), Kenya's natural forest resources face immense pressure.

High demand for raw materials, land conversion, infrastructure development, and socio-economic challenges like poverty drive this threat. Forests, vital for ecosystem balance, biodiversity, and livelihoods, are severely endangered. A notable gap persists between policy discussions on ecosystem services and actual community involvement.

TEAMEnvironment KENY A aims to close this gap by establishing 1,000,000 tree nurseries, seedling propagation, and environmental resource centers across all 47 Kenyan counties, directly engaging and empowering communities. Kenya consumes approximately 80 million trees annually but requires 450 million for sustainable forest management.

This deficit is worsened by a heavy reliance on biomass energy, as charcoal and firewood constitute about 70% of primary energy consumption. Widespread deforestation, degradation, and rampant forest fires have severely impacted critical water towers like Mount Kenya, Mau Forest, and the Aberdare Ranges. Charcoal and firewood collectively account for about 70% of primary energy consumption.

Despite the government's recent ban on illegal logging and forest product extraction, timber scarcity has driven up demand and prices. Biomass energy consumption remains high and is even rising, fueled by poverty, population growth, and urbanization. The illegal charcoal industry, estimated at KES 40 to 80 billion (USD 4003800 million) annually, thrives due to corruption.

This, combined with industrial woody biomass use and overgrazing in the Rift Valley, places immense strain on natural resources and encroaches upon rich biodiversity. Kenya's forest cover plummeted from 20% at independence in 1963 to a mere 2% in the 1990s. While restoration efforts have raised it to 8.2%, this remains below the 10% UN recommended minimum and the 12. 16% global convention target.

Kenya's Vision 2030 aims to plant 360 million trees annually, targeting over 5 million hectares of additional forest cover through the 15 Billion T ree Growing Agenda by 2032. T o achieve this, 70% of new forest cover will result from reforestation, afforestation, and tree farm planting, with the remaining 30% from natural regeneration.

Environmental rights and actions are enshrined in Article 42 of the Constitution of Kenya 2010, alongside other policy frameworks, mandating proactive conservation efforts to meet Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Integrating sustainable forest resource development, management, and conservation is vital for enriching biodiversity and ensuring the provision of essential ecosystem goods and services for domestic and industrial utilization.

Programme Development & Implementation Phase 1: Nursery Establishment We establish nurseries in optimal locations (schools, institutions, public/private lands) with reliable water and security. KFS and KEFRI guide the selection of indigenous, exotic, and non-invasive species for cultural, ornamental, nutritional, medicinal, conservation, and restoration purposes.

Phase 2: Logistics & Support We provide volunteers with meals, transport, and accommodation, ensuring their full participation in nationwide tree planting (growing) across all 47 counties. Emergency services are available as needed throughout the program.

Phase 3: Facility Management TEK collaborates with the local communities to establish and manage tree nurseries and the planting of trees nurturing them to maturity. One million nurseries across the 47 counties will increase the tree and forest cover inline with the TEK's Sustainable Landscape Environment Restoration Program (SLERP) to build climate resilience.

Phase 4: Resource Centre Development Nurseries evolve into resource centers, scaling capacity for diverse plants (trees, shrubs, grasses). These centers serve multiple functions: conservation, carbon sequestration, biomass production, medicinal, cultural, nutritional, fodder , building materials, energy, shade, and ornamental.

We prioritize indigenous and exotic non-invasive species, using local resources to reduce costs. CONCLUSION As TEAMEnvironment KENY A, we are dedicated to leaving a lasting heritage for future generations: a cleaner , greener (food & water) secure, and peaceful environment thriving with diverse flora, fauna, and aquatic life.

This duty, mandate, and conservation responsibility cannot be abdicated or delegated; it rests with all of us. T o this vital cause, our clarion call is: "Let's Go Green With Y ou.
